arxiv-1905-09752.title: Measurement of distributions sensitive to the underlying event in inclusive Z-boson production in pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1905-09752.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1905-09752.description: Abstract This paper presents measurements of charged-particle distributions sensitive to the properties of the underlying event in events containing a Z Z boson decaying into a muon pair. The data were obtained using the ATLAS detector at the LHC in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with an integrated luminosity of 3.2 fb -1 .

arxiv-1905-11810.title: Meissner-like effect and conductivity of power-Maxwell holographic superconductors
arxiv-1905-11810.creator: Doa Hashemi Asl, Ahmad Sheykhi
arxiv-1905-11810.description: Abstract The full description of a superconductor requires that it has an infinite DC conductivity (or zero electrical resistivity) as well as expels the external magnetic fields. Thus, for any holographic superconductor which is dual to a real superconductor, it is necessary to examine, simultaneously, these two features based on the gauge/gravity duality.

arxiv-1911-05636.title: Prevalence of code mixing in semi-formal patient communication in low resource languages of South Africa
arxiv-1911-05636.creator: Dr Monika Obrocka, Dr Charles Copley, Themba Gqaza, Dr Eli Grant
arxiv-1911-05636.description: Abstract In this paper we address the problem of code-mixing in resource-poor language settings. We examine data consisting of 182k unique questions generated by users of the MomConnect helpdesk, part of a national scale public health platform in South Africa.

arxiv-2102-10240.title: Learning Neural Generative Dynamics for Molecular Conformation Generation
arxiv-2102-10240.creator: Minkai Xu*, Shitong Luo*, Yoshua Bengio, Jian Peng, Jian Tang
arxiv-2102-10240.description: Abstract We study how to generate molecule conformations ( i.e. , 3D structures) from a molecular graph. Traditional methods, such as molecular dynamics, sample conformations via computationally expensive simulations. Recently, machine learning methods have shown great potential by training on a large collection of conformation data.

arxiv-2104-06807.title: Stochastic geometry analysis of a distance-based JT scheme in C-RAN
arxiv-2104-06807.creator: Charles Wiame, Claude Oestges, and Luc Vandendorpe
arxiv-2104-06807.description: Abstract This paper considers a joint transmission scheme (JT) developed for cloud radio access networks (C-RANs). This proposed scheme features cooperative sets of remote radio heads (RRH) defined in a disk around each user location. The nodes belonging to each of these sets perform a weighted maximum ratio transmission to jointly serve the user.

arxiv-2108-09064.title: Intersection spaces and multiple transverse recurrence
arxiv-2108-09064.creator: Michael Björklund, Tobias Hartnick, Yakov Karasik
arxiv-2108-09064.description: Abstract . We study multiple recurrence properties along separated cross sections for pmp actions of unimodular lcsc group on Polish spaces. We establish a multiple transverse recurrence theorem under the assumption that sufficiently large powers of the return time set are Delone sets. Typical examples of such situations arise from the theory of uniform approximate lattices.

arxiv-2112-03791.title: Online Sorting and Translational Packing of Convex Polygons This paper was presented at the ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA23).
arxiv-2112-03791.creator: Anonymous, Anders Aamand †, Mikkel Abrahamsen †, Lorenzo Beretta †, Linda Kleist †
arxiv-2112-03791.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anonymous, Anders Aamand †, Mikkel Abrahamsen †, Lorenzo Beretta †, Linda Kleist †. We investigate several online packing problems in which convex polygons arrive one by one and have to be placed irrevocably into a container, while the aim is to minimize the used space.

arxiv-2204-03050.title: Investigation of Δ 0 ​ Δ 0 \Delta^{0}\Delta^{0} dibaryon in QCD
arxiv-2204-03050.creator: H. Mutuk, K. Azizi
arxiv-2204-03050.description: Abstract We study a hypothetical Δ 0 ​ Δ 0 \Delta^{0}\Delta^{0} dibaryon state by means of QCD sum rule method. We construct a scalar interpolating current to extract the mass and decay constant of this state taking into account contributions of various quark, gluon and mixed vacuum condensates.

arxiv-2305-00943.title: On the non-abelian Hodge locus I
arxiv-2305-00943.creator: Philip Engel, Salim Tayou
arxiv-2305-00943.description: Abstract . We partially resolve conjectures of Deligne and Simpson concerning ℤ {\mathbb{Z}} -local systems on quasi-projective varieties that underlie a polarized variation of Hodge structure. For local systems of “compact type”, we prove (1) a relative form of Deligne’s finiteness theorem, for any family of quasi-projective varieties, and (2) algebraicity of the corresponding non-abelian Hodge locus. 1.

arxiv-2305-10168.title: Long Memory of Max-Stable Time Series as Phase Transition: Asymptotic Behaviour of Tail Dependence Estimators
arxiv-2305-10168.creator: Marco Oesting, Albert Rapp ??
arxiv-2305-10168.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a simple estimator for tail dependence coefficients of a max-stable time series and show its asymptotic normality under a mild condition. The novelty of our result is that this condition does not involve mixing properties that are common in the literature.

arxiv-2309-15844.title: Data-Driven Framework for Uncovering Hidden Control Strategies in Evolutionary Analysis
arxiv-2309-15844.creator: Nourddine Azzaoui, Tomoko Matsui, Daisuke Murakami
arxiv-2309-15844.description: Abstract We have devised a data-driven framework for uncovering hidden control strategies used by an evolutionary system described by an evolutionary probability distribution. This innovative framework enables deciphering of the concealed mechanisms that contribute to the progression or mitigation of such situations as the spread of COVID-19.

arxiv-2310-01766.title: Learning Causal Alignment for Reliable Disease Diagnosis
arxiv-2310-01766.creator: Mingzhou Liu Ching-Wen Lee Xinwei Sun Xueqing Yu Qiao Yu Yizhou Wang
arxiv-2310-01766.description: Abstract Aligning the decision-making process of machine learning algorithms with that of experienced radiologists is crucial for reliable diagnosis. While existing methods have attempted to align their diagnosis behaviors to those of radiologists reflected in the training data, this alignment is primarily associational rather than causal, resulting in pseudo-correlations that may not transfer well.

arxiv-2412-16921.title: 3D Radiative MHD Simulations of Starspots II: Large-scale Structure
arxiv-2412-16921.creator: Tanayveer Singh Bhatia ,, Mayukh Panja, Robert H. Cameron, Sami K. Solanki
arxiv-2412-16921.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tanayveer Singh Bhatia ,, Mayukh Panja, Robert H. Cameron, Sami K. Solanki. We compute realistic 3D radiative MHD near-surface models of starspots with substantial penumbrae on cool main-sequence stars using the MURaM simulation code. This work is an improvement on the the previous starspot models in a slab geometry. The umbra, penumbra and the quiet star for all starspots are distinct, not only in intensity and temperature, but also in thermodynamic and velocity structure.

arxiv-2502-09736.title: Coherent lidar for ride-hailing autonomous vehicles
arxiv-2502-09736.creator: Alexander Y. Piggott, Cathy Yunshan Jiang, John Lam, Blaise Gassend, Simon Verghese
arxiv-2502-09736.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexander Y. Piggott, Cathy Yunshan Jiang, John Lam, Blaise Gassend, Simon Verghese. Coherent lidars promise a number of advantages over traditional time-of-flight lidars for autonomous vehicles. These include the direct measurement of target approach velocities via the Doppler effect, and near-immunity to interference from other lidars and sunlight. Furthermore, coherent lidars are compatible with a variety of solid-state beam steering technologies such as optical phased arrays, which may enable low-cost and compact lidars.

arxiv-2508-20674.title: Bridging Minds and Machines: Toward an Integration of AI and Cognitive Science
arxiv-2508-20674.creator: Rui Mao, Qian Liu, Xiao Li, Erik Cambria, Amir Hussain
arxiv-2508-20674.description: Abstract Cognitive Science has profoundly shaped disciplines such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Philosophy, Psychology, Neuroscience, Linguistics, and Culture. Many breakthroughs in AI trace their roots to cognitive theories, while AI itself has become an indispensable tool for advancing cognitive research. This reciprocal relationship motivates a comprehensive review of the intersections between AI and Cognitive Science.

arxiv-2602-19239.title: Attention Deficits in Language Models: Causal Explanations for Procedural Hallucinations
arxiv-2602-19239.creator: Ahmed Karim, Fatima Sheaib, Zein Khamis, Maggie Chlon, Jad Awada, Leon Chlon
arxiv-2602-19239.description: Abstract Large language models can follow complex procedures yet fail at a seemingly trivial final step: reporting a value they themselves computed moments earlier. We study this as procedural hallucination : failure to execute a verifiable, prompt-grounded specification even when the correct value is present in-context.

arxiv-2603-26948.title: Compliance-Aware Predictive Process Monitoring: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach
arxiv-2603-26948.creator: Fabrizio De Santis✉, Gyunam Park, Wil M.P. van der Aalst, Francesco Zanichelli

arxiv-2606-26097.title: Positron-Emitting and Electron-Capturing Double-Beta Processes in the Standard Model and Beyond
arxiv-2606-26097.creator: Lukáš Gráf, Jenni Kotila, Oliver Scholer

britannica-1911-montchretien-antoine-de.title: Montchrétien, Antoine de (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-montchretien-antoine-de.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-montchretien-antoine-de.description: Article 'Montchrétien, Antoine de' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. dramatist and economist, son of an apothecary at Falaise named Mauchrestien, was born about 1576. In one of his numerous duels he had the misfortune to kill his opponent. He consequently took refuge in England, but through the influence of James I., to whom he dedicated his tragedy, L’Écossaise, he was allowed to return to France, and established himself at Auxonne-sur-Loire, where he set up a steel foundry.

europmc-pmc6688448.title: Measuring shared responses across subjects using intersubject correlation.
europmc-pmc6688448.creator: Nastase SA, Gazzola V, Hasson U, Keysers C.
europmc-pmc6688448.description: Our capacity to jointly represent information about the world underpins our social experience. By leveraging one individual's brain activity to model another's, we can measure shared information across brains-even in dynamic, naturalistic scenarios where an explicit response...

pmc-10544595.title: Association of diabetes risk reduction diet with renal cancer risk in 101,755 participants: a prospective study
pmc-10544595.creator: Ling Xiang, Yi Xiao, Zhiquan Xu, Haoyun Luo, Xiaorui Ren, Qi Wei, Zhiyong Zhu, Yahui Jiang, Yunhao Tang, Hongmei He, Zhihang Zhou, Haitao Gu, Yaxu Wang, Linglong Peng
pmc-10544595.description: BackgroundThere is little prospective evidence exists about whether adherence to a diabetes risk reduction diet (DRRD) is related to a significant reduction in renal cancer risk. We sought to clarify whether adherence to DRRD was associated with a reduced risk of renal cancer in a US population.

pmc-10736471.title: EARLY-LIFE EXPOSURE TO THE GREAT DEPRESSION AND THE PACE OF BIOLOGICAL AGING
pmc-10736471.creator: Lauren Schmitz
pmc-10736471.description: The Developmental Origins of Health and Disease hypothesis proposes that insults to early-life development can result in increased risk for aging-related disease later in life. There is growing interest within gerontology in the potential role such early life exposures play in shaping processes of aging. However, causal research linking early-life exposures to processes of aging in later life is rare.

pmc-11360154.title: Risk Assessment of Displaced Sediment by an Extreme Event Cyclone in a Peri-Urban Zone Using Bioassays and Analytical Chemistry
pmc-11360154.creator: Louis A. Tremblay, Daisuke Nakajima, Satoshi Endo, Mayuko Yagishita, Hannah Ludlow, Ariana Mackay, Olivier Champeau
pmc-11360154.description: Hawke’s Bay in New Zealand was impacted by Cyclone Gabrielle in 2023, experiencing intense weather conditions and rainfall. Rivers and streams surged beyond their banks, displacing large amounts of sediment. The sewage treatment plant and industries in the Waitangi catchment, south of the city of Napier, were heavily impacted, making them potential sources of contaminants.

pmc-11367032.title: Performance studies of an ultrafast gamma Cherenkov imaging Screen based on Silica fibers array
pmc-11367032.creator: Zhang Mei, Yang Li, Yan Song, Liang Sheng, Quan Guo, Yi Hong Yan, Hong Qiao Yin
pmc-11367032.description: High-energy gamma rays produced in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments are crucial for studying implosion dynamics. These gamma rays, characterized by their extremely short durations, represent the least disturbed products of fusion, preserving vital birth information. To detect such γ-rays, ultrafast radiation detectors with high time resolution are necessary.

pmc-11406818.title: Joint effects of ill-health, health shocks and social protection on the intensive margin of labour supply: evidence from Malawi
pmc-11406818.creator: Ken Chamuva Shawa, Bruce Hollingsworth, Eugenio Zucchelli
pmc-11406818.description: BackgroundThere is sparse evidence on the joint effects of ill-health, health shocks and social protection on the intensive margin of labour supply, particularly in developing countries. We interact ill-health and health shocks with access to social protection and estimate their joint effects on weekly hours of work.

pmc-11518278.title: Long COVID Prevalence and Factors Among ethnically Diverse UK Healthcare Workers
pmc-11518278.creator: A Al-Oraibi, CAA Martin, K Woolf, L Bryant, L B Nellums, C Tarrant, K Khunti, M Pareek
pmc-11518278.description: BackgroundLong COVID (LC), characterised by persistent symptoms post-acute COVID-19 infection, presents a growing public health concern. Data on prevalence among healthcare workers (HCWs) are lacking. Our study aimed to establish the proportion of UK HCWs with symptoms lasting beyond five weeks and identify factors associated with LC in a diverse cohort.

pmc-11532238.title: The role of sodium in the electrochemical tuning of Li2TiSiO5 anodes across ceramic and glass phases
pmc-11532238.creator: Awadol Khejonrak, Amorntep Montreeuppathum, Sumeth Siriroj, Jintara Padchasri, Sarawut Pasee, Narong Chanlek, Soorathep Kheawhom, Pinit Kidkhunthod
pmc-11532238.description: This study investigates the enhancement of Li2TiSiO5 anode material through Na doping via two routes: melt-quenching (route I) and subsequent heat treatment (route II). A 5 % Na-doped ceramic sample significantly improves Li-ion mobility and discharge capacity (215 mA h g−1 at 10 mA g−1), sustaining 45 mA h g−1 at a high rate of 1 A g−1.

pmc-11613722.title: Evaluating COVID-19 impact, vaccination, birth registration, and underreporting in a predominantly indigenous population in Chiapas, Mexico
pmc-11613722.creator: Elienai Joaquin-Damas, Svenn-Erik Mamelund, Benjamin M Schnneider, Beatriz E Sánchez-Hernández, Amanda Patishtán-López, Amanda Bleichrodt, Gerardo Chowell
pmc-11613722.description: Background Indigenous populations globally face significant health disparities compared to non-Indigenous groups, primarily due to marginalization and limited access to healthcare. In Mexico, which is home to the largest Indigenous population in the Americas, these disparities were further exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, with impacts intensified by factors such as marginalization, discrimination, and inadequate access to essential services.

pmc-11644861.title: Effect of Alkali Source on Crystal Regulation and Ethanol Gas Sensing Properties of Nano-ZnO
pmc-11644861.creator: Yinying Liao, Lu Qiu, Yunfei Ouyang, Dayang Feng, Shiyi Huang, Zhaoyang Zhang, Xinyao Xie, Junwei Ke, Tianhao Liu, Xiangxiang Chen, Hongshan Bi, Weiran Zuo
pmc-11644861.description: This study investigates the ethanol gas-sensing mechanisms of ZnO nanocrystals with distinct morphologies, synthesized via a hydrothermal method using various alkali sources. Significant differences in the gas-sensing performance and morphology of ZnO samples synthesized with ammonium carbonate (Na2CO3), hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA), ammonia solution (NH3·H2O), and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) were observed.

pmc-12172941.title: Pairing explainable deep learning classification with clustering to uncover effects of schizophrenia upon whole brain functional network connectivity dynamics
pmc-12172941.creator: Charles A Ellis, Robyn L Miller, Vince D Calhoun
pmc-12172941.description: Many studies have analyzed resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC) data to elucidate the effects of neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders upon the interactions of brain regions over time. Existing studies often use either machine learning classification or clustering algorithms.

pmc-13194405.title: Development and validation of a comprehensive prevention-focused intervention package for problematic digital technology use among youth: a multi-site study protocol
pmc-13194405.creator: Yatan Pal Singh Balhara, Vishal Dhiman, Siddharth Sarkar, Rajeev Ranjan, Rachna Bhargava, Ragul Ganesh, Shivanand Kattimani, Bichitra Nanda Patra, Syed Hubbe Ali, Audrey Gogoi
pmc-13194405.description: BackgroundProblematic use of digital technology among children, adolescents, and young adults is associated with adverse health, behavioural, interpersonal, social, academic and vocational outcomes. Most existing research focuses on treatment oriented interventions. Prevention focused interventions are limited. This is especially true for the low- and middle-income countries. There is a need for structured prevention approaches that involve youth, parents, and teachers.

pmc-13224245.title: Prophylactic oxytocin infusion for reducing blood loss during elective caesarean delivery: A randomised controlled trial
pmc-13224245.creator: Praveena Govindan, Jyotsna Sharma, Kubera N.S., Pankaj Kundra, Dilip Kumar Maurya, Anish Keepanasseril
pmc-13224245.description: Background and objectivesOptimum dose, route, and timing of oxytocin administration to prevent postpartum haemorrhage during caesarean section are uncertain. We compared the effect of oxytocin infusion initiated either at skin incision or after head delivery on blood loss and ease of foetal head delivery during elective caesarean section.
